findings.title: Reentrancy Vulnerability in VulnerableBank.withdraw()
findings.description: External call to msg.sender.call{value: balance}() occurs before state variable balances[msg.sender] is set to 0. An attacker can re-enter withdraw() before the balance is zeroed.
findings.impact: Complete drainage of contract ETH. Attacker can recursively call withdraw() to drain all funds.
findings.fix_suggestion: Use OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard, or apply checks-effects-interactions pattern: set balances[msg.sender] = 0 BEFORE the external call.

findings.title: Reentrancy in VulnerableAMM.flashLoan() — Balance Read Stale
findings.description: Balance is read via tokenA.balanceOf(address(this)) before external call tokenA.transfer(). After the transfer, the stale balanceBefore variable is used in the repayment check, which can be manipulated via reentrancy.
findings.impact: Flash loan repayment bypass: attacker can re-enter flashLoan() before repayment check, allowing unrepaid loans.
findings.fix_suggestion: Use a reentrancy guard, or re-read balance after transfer and compare against expected minimum, not a stale snapshot.

findings.title: Reentrancy in VulnerableAMM.swapAtoB() — State Written After External Calls
findings.description: External calls to tokenA.transferFrom() and tokenB.transfer() occur before reserveA and reserveB state variables are updated. An attacker with a malicious token contract can re-enter and exploit stale reserves.
findings.impact: Price manipulation and fund theft through swap with stale reserves.
findings.fix_suggestion: Update reserveA and reserveB BEFORE making external token transfers. Use ReentrancyGuard as additional protection.

findings.title: Unchecked ERC20 Return Values (5 instances)
findings.description: Multiple ERC20 transfer/transferFrom calls ignore the return value. If the token returns false on failure instead of reverting, the operation silently fails.
findings.impact: Liquidity added without actual token transfer, swaps executed without actual token movement, flash loans disbursed without verification.
findings.fix_suggestion: Use OpenZeppelin SafeERC20 library: `using SafeERC20 for IERC20;` and call `safeTransfer`/`safeTransferFrom`.

findings.title: Low-Level Call Usage
findings.description: Low-level call msg.sender.call{value: balance}() is used to send ETH. While the return value is checked, low-level calls bypass Solidity's type system.
findings.impact: Reentrancy vector and potential for unexpected behavior if called by a contract without receive/fallback.
findings.fix_suggestion: Consider using Address.sendValue() from OpenZeppelin, or at minimum ensure no state changes after the call.

findings.title: State Variables Should Be Immutable
findings.description: tokenA and tokenB state variables are set only in the constructor and never modified. They should be declared immutable to save gas.
findings.impact: Minor gas inefficiency. No security impact.
findings.fix_suggestion: Declare as `IERC20 public immutable tokenA;` and `IERC20 public immutable tokenB;`.

findings.title: Solc Version Contains Known Issues
findings.description: Version constraint ^0.8.0 contains known severe compiler bugs including DirtyBytesArrayToStorage, SignedImmutables, and others.
findings.impact: Potential compiler-level bugs in edge cases.
findings.fix_suggestion: Pin to a specific patched version: `pragma solidity 0.8.20;` or higher.

findings.title: ETH Transferred Without Address Checks
findings.description: ETH is transferred to addresses without verifying msg.sender identity. Consider introducing checks for msg.sender to ensure the recipient is as intended.
findings.fix_suggestion: Add msg.sender checks and access control before ETH transfers.

findings.title: Unchecked Return Values
findings.description: Function returns a value but it is ignored. Consider checking the return value.
findings.fix_suggestion: Always check return values of external calls and token operations.

findings.title: Address State Variable Set Without Zero-Address Checks
findings.description: Check for address(0) when assigning values to address state variables.
findings.fix_suggestion: Add `require(addr != address(0))` checks before setting address state variables.

findings.title: Unsafe ERC20 Operations
findings.description: ERC20 functions may not behave as expected. Return values are not always meaningful. Use OpenZeppelin's SafeERC20 library.
findings.fix_suggestion: Use SafeERC20 for all token operations.
